name: Black Breath
label: Southern Lord
lede: Two Bellingham friends buy Boss HM-2 pedals, run Swedish death metal through a hardcore band, and end up on Southern Lord with Kurt Ballou at the board for all three albums. Then the band goes quiet, and the story gets sadder before it gets a coda.

eras.title: Bellingham, then Seattle
eras.text: Black Breath starts in a college town north of Seattle, puts out its own first EP on its own label, and moves south. The sound is crust and hardcore with Swedish death metal buzzsaw guitars laid on top.

years.src: Bara Metal on Sentenced to Life · Black Breath (band), Wikipedia
years.h: Zack Muljat and Jamie Byrum start a band in Bellingham
years.p: [[Neil McAdams|ceeaf6f3-14d9-4097-8b69-3f0d997148fa]] sings. The name comes from a Repulsion song that [[Entombed|61b99cc4-06cd-4ad5-9bac-950b2daef9cc]] later covered, and not from Tolkien.
years.xp:
Guitarist Muljat and drummer Byrum found the band in winter 2005, per the sources available. Dates for the early lineup vary.

Bara Metal traces the name to the Repulsion song "Black Breath," and says it did not come from Tolkien.

years.h: Eric Wallace brings a second guitar, Elijah Nelson takes bass
years.p: That settles the band that will make its Southern Lord records. Sources date both arrivals to 2007.

years.h: Razor to Oblivion comes out on the band's own Hot Mass label
years.p: A short, fast EP, pressed by the band itself. It is the record that gets Southern Lord looking.
years.xp: Sources give the date as January or November 2008, and describe it as four or five tracks. Southern Lord signed the band in October 2009 and the EP was later reissued on the label.

years.h: The band packs up and moves from Bellingham to Seattle
years.p: The move comes in early 2008, the same year as the first EP.

eras.title: Southern Lord calls
eras.text: The label behind Sunn O))) and Goatsnake signs the band, and Black Breath heads to Massachusetts to record with Kurt Ballou.

years.p: The Los Angeles label, run by [[Greg Anderson|a8da7651-6d6f-4021-98a6-d68b35b1e4f8]], also reissues the Razor to Oblivion EP.

years.h: Heavy Breathing goes to Salem to meet Kurt Ballou
years.p: Ballou of [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]] records the debut at his GodCity studio, and the Boss HM-2 guitar tone sits at the front.
years.xp: Twelve tracks, produced by Ballou at his GodCity Studio. Ballou would record all three of the band's Southern Lord albums.

years.cap: Black Breath live in Seattle, August 2010
years.h: First US tours, on bills with Trap Them, Victims and Rise and Fall
years.p: The band tours the States behind Heavy Breathing, sharing stages with [[Trap Them|b24b6ae8-333e-4351-b3b7-6be843195a16]] among others.

eras.title: Sentenced to Life
eras.text: A guitar swap, then the second album, the one that gets the band noticed beyond the hardcore world.

years.h: Founding guitarist Zack Muljat steps out, Mark Palm steps in
years.p: Sources put the change in 2011 or 2012, and say Muljat left to study law. Palm takes the guitar for the rest of the band's run.

years.src: Bara Metal on Sentenced to Life
years.h: Sentenced to Life picks up a tenth song at the last minute
years.p: Ten songs, including "Home of the Grave" and "Mother Abyss," again made with [[Kurt Ballou|1e922902-2cb9-499f-aeb5-9a8c51dd0df0]] at GodCity.
years.xp:
The band told Bara Metal it nearly stopped at nine songs. Then Eric Wallace wrote the verse music for "The Flame" at midnight, "getting drunk at the hotel," and the intro and outro riffs came together in seconds before the drums were tracked. Much of the lyric writing happened in hotel rooms between 2 and 5 AM.

A harmonized guitar part in "Of Flesh" ate an afternoon for barely a second and a half of music. The band joked about the "$200 riff."

The cover is a sledgehammer smashing glass, held in Wallace's own hand. The band had looked at Kill 'Em All, British Steel and Black Flag's Damaged, planned a chrome gavel first, and decided the sledgehammer was "way more menacing."

years.big: I think I own three, but we probably have six between us.
years.src: Bara Metal on Sentenced to Life
years.h: A pedal that breaks, so the band keeps spares
years.p: A band member on the Boss HM-2, the distortion pedal behind the Swedish death metal sound, to Bara Metal. The reason for the backups: "Shit breaks, you know?"
years.xp: The HM-2 is the pink Boss pedal that gives [[Entombed|61b99cc4-06cd-4ad5-9bac-950b2daef9cc]] and the Stockholm bands their buzzsaw tone, and the band's records lean on it. Spares are standard equipment on the road.

eras.title: Slaves Beyond Death
eras.text: Festival sets, club tours and a third album that sounds more like old heavy metal than hardcore.

years.cap: Neil McAdams at Saint Vitus, Brooklyn, December 2014
years.h: A third album is announced, with Ballou back at GodCity
years.p: Southern Lord makes the announcement in October. The record was cut over the winter in Salem, Massachusetts.

years.src: Ghost Cult interview · No Echo review
yt: Full set, Saint Vitus Bar, Brooklyn, July 2015
years.h: Slaves Beyond Death turns toward old-school metal
years.p: Eight songs. Neil McAdams tells Ghost Cult there is "way more guitar," and Jamie Byrum says the vocals "aren't hardcore vocals."
years.xp:
McAdams puts it as a different approach for a different kind of record, with the guitars rooted in old-school heavy metal and hard rock rather than death metal.

The band toured with Goatwhore that summer and, per Ghost Cult, ran into a truck carrying uranium hexafluoride in Utah. Ghost Cult also mentions a US tour with Decapitated planned for 2016.

eras.title: Quiet, then a loss and a box set
eras.text: Black Breath goes silent after 2015. In December 2019 its bassist dies, and Southern Lord boxes up the records.

years.src: Blabbermouth on Elijah Nelson · New Noise: the return of Black Breath
years.p: He died over the weekend of December 28-29, 2019, and no cause was made public. Nasum called him "the Cliff Burton of death metal."
years.xp:
Blabbermouth reported the news, noting the band had been largely inactive for about three years. Nasum, whom Black Breath had played with on the final leg of Nasum's farewell tour, wrote that Black Breath "were very important" to them on it.

In 2026 Neil McAdams told New Noise: "Elijah wouldn't want us to stop playing forever." Jamie Byrum said: "There hasn't been a band practice where we don't end up getting into an Elijah riff."

years.cap: Black Breath at Northwest Terror Fest, Seattle
years.src: New Noise: the return of Black Breath
yt: I Am Beyond, Northwest Terror Fest, June 2026
years.h: Southern Lord boxes up the whole discography on vinyl
years.p: The set gathers all of Black Breath's records, released May 3, 2024.
years.xp:
In June 2026 Byrum and McAdams, with guitarist Cliff Martin, played a one-off reunion set at Neumos during Northwest Terror Fest. They had turned the festival down for three years, New Noise reports.

Asked about more shows and new songs, Byrum answered "Yes and yes."
